Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re well. I lead partner strategy at OpenHorizon Labs; we publish a family of open models and are exploring controlled distribution partnerships for full weights (non-commercial & commercial tiers). We’ve seen Redwood referenced repeatedly by customers for production-grade serving and want to discuss a pilot to make our weights available via a restricted mirror/hosting partnership.

High-level asks from our side:

Team,

Forwarding Ava’s materials. Quick internal take before the call Monday:

- Commercial model: rev-share works but we should prefer a minimum guaranteed commit for Dedicated pools; otherwise model-hosting revenue can be noisy.
- Access controls: allowlist + signed attestation is fine; we should push for token-based billing visibility per-customer and an audit endpoint for request provenance.
- Embargo: 7 days is reasonable. For new major releases (e.g., v2.0), request staged rollouts with canary windows.
- IP/license: avoid clauses that restrict us from offering optimizations/quantization; need explicit carve-outs for inference optimizations we apply.

Can Marissa and Camila propose redlines to the attached hosting_offer.xlsx and the PDF? Camila, please focus on license carve-outs and audit rights; Marissa on ops/onboarding checklist and commercial floor.

Also note: OpenHorizon asked about mirror-only vs hosted API. We should show both options in the pilot proposal (hosted API first, mirror + dedicated for enterprise).

Sergio
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Sergio / team,

Attached a short redline summary and recommended clause language. High-level proposed edits:

1) License scope  define explicit downstream rights for inference-only hosting; carve out rights to optimize/quantize/compile for inference (we should be able to modify model weights for performance without being treated as a derivative work).
2) Audit & logs  agree to 180 days by default, add an audit clause allowing OpenHorizon to request a one-time audit with 30 days notice for compliance issues (for pilot only, customer-paid for recurring audits).
3) Embargo & release cadence  allow for staged canary releases; for major releases require a minimum 3-day coordination window and a 14-day maximum embargo for coordinated commercial launch (OpenHorizon keeps right to shorten).
4) Attribution & watermarking  require model card metadata surface but avoid mandatory watermarking in responses; allow observational telemetry for misuse detection.
5) Rev-share & guarantees  recommend a pilot with revenue split but include a minimum monthly guarantee for dedicated pools; we propose 5k-10k USD floor depending on expected QPS.

I attached redline_summary.docx (summary + clause snippets). If you approve, I can prepare a tracked redline of their Drive draft and send to Ava with our questions.

Camila Reyes
Senior Counsel, Platform & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
